sections.md:
**MONITORING**

Two events, both dated May 27, 2026, have reset the LEED transition calendar and elevated the signal for any workspace serving clients in the construction, fit-out, or building operations supply chain.

**The registration deadline extension.** FACT: "USGBC has extended the LEED v4 and LEED v4.1 commercial registration close date from June 30, 2026 to June 30, 2027." *Source: LEED v4 and v4.1 commercial registration close extended to June 30, 2027, U.S. Green Building Council (USGBC), May 27, 2026. https://www.usgbc.org/articles/leed-v4-and-v41-commercial-registration-close-extended-june-30-2027

FACT: The stated reason is direct market feedback: "USGBC members and project teams have shared that market conditions—including supply chain constraints, financing challenges and regulatory uncertainty—are affecting project timelines." *Source: LEED v4 and v4.1 commercial registration close extended to June 30, 2027, USGBC, May 27, 2026. https://www.usgbc.org/articles/leed-v4-and-v41-commercial-registration-close-extended-june-30-2027

*Operational implication:* The one-year extension signals that a material portion of the global LEED project pipeline — particularly projects in markets with supply chain stress — is not moving at the pace USGBC originally projected. For workspaces moving construction and fit-out freight, this extends the window during which v4/v4.1 compliance documentation governs client procurement decisions, but it also compresses the gap between the current date and the now-confirmed July 1, 2027 v5 hard switchover.

**The LEED v5 hard cutover date.** FACT: "Starting on July 1, 2027, LEED v5 will be the only version available for new registrations for the commercial LEED BD+C, ID+C, and O+M rating systems, with limited exceptions." *Source: LEED v5, U.S. Green Building Council Help Center, updated May 28, 2026. https://support.usgbc.org/hc/en-us/articles/25316160948755-LEED-v5

**The certification sunset.** FACT: The certification sunset date for LEED v4 and v4.1 across all commercial rating systems — BD+C, ID+C, O+M, Recertification, and O+M: Interiors — is June 30, 2033. *Source: LEED certification deadlines, USGBC. https://www.usgbc.org/tools/leed-certification/deadlines

**LEED v5 certification is already open.** FACT: LEED v5 project registration is now available in Arc for LEED v5 BD+C: New Construction, BD+C: Core and Shell, ID+C: Commercial Interiors, and O+M: Existing Buildings. *Source: LEED v5, USGBC Help Center, updated May 28, 2026. https://support.usgbc.org/hc/en-us/articles/25316160948755-LEED-v5

**LEED v5 for Cities is in active public comment.** FACT: "The second public comment period opened on May 14, 2026 and will close June 16, 2026." *Source: LEED v5, USGBC Help Center, updated May 28, 2026. https://support.usgbc.org/hc/en-us/articles/25316160948755-LEED-v5

*Analytical inference:* The Cities rating system — covering municipal and district-scale projects — is approximately one public comment cycle behind the commercial rating systems, placing it on a trajectory for ratification in late 2026 or 2027. Workspaces serving urban infrastructure or large-scale mixed-use clients should monitor this track separately from the BD+C/ID+C/O+M track.

---

**Action 1 — Identify LEED-active clients and map their version status.**
Before the July 2027 switchover, the workspace's client base will be split across v4, v4.1, and v5 projects simultaneously. Build a simple client-project register noting which LEED version governs each project and which registration deadline applies. This is zero-cost intelligence that directly informs documentation and reporting priorities.

**Action 2 — Pull the LEED v5 credit library and read the transport-relevant credits.**
FACT: The LEED credit library now includes "dozens of USGBC-created calculators to support credit documentation." *Source: LEED v5 expands: New Arc certification tools and resources for users, CAGBC/USGBC, November 3, 2025. https://www.cagbc.org/news-resources/cagbc-news/leed-v5-expands-new-arc-certification-tools-and-resources-for-users/ The credit library is publicly accessible at https://www.usgbc.org/leed/v5 (listed in New Sources Identified). Reading the transport and materials credits directly — rather than through intermediary summaries — is the only way to understand what documentation the workspace may be asked to produce.

**Action 3 — Evaluate the beta credentialing window.**
FACT: LEED Green Associate beta exam is available April 28–June 30, 2026, at 30% discount; LEED AP with Specialty June 30–August 31, 2026. *Source: LEED v5 beta exams to launch in 2026, GBCI, January 29, 2026. https://www.gbci.org/leed-v5-beta-exams-launch-2026 For sustainability, commercial, or operations staff who are already LEED Green Associates or LEED APs under v4, the beta window is a low-cost entry point to v5 content fluency before the standard exam launches. This is particularly relevant for commercial and client-facing roles that will be fielding LEED v5 questions from clients.

**Action 4 — Add LEED v5 transport documentation as a standing item on the emissions reporting development roadmap.**
*Operational implication:* The direction of travel — LEED v5 project impact reports covering transportation, with metrics on emissions — is sourced. The specific data format requirements are not yet confirmed. The right action now is to ensure the workspace's emissions reporting infrastructure (Scope 3 transport emissions, carrier data, last-mile mode documentation) is on the development agenda with the July 2027 switchover as the target readiness date.

**Action 5 — Monitor the LEED v5 for Cities second comment period outcome.**
FACT: The second public comment period closes June 16, 2026. *Source: LEED v5, USGBC Help Center, updated May 28, 2026. https://support.usgbc.org/hc/en-us/articles/25316160948755-LEED-v5 For workspaces serving urban infrastructure or municipal clients, the Cities track ratification timeline is the relevant next event. Re-check after June 16, 2026 for USGBC's publication of next steps.

**Re-check window:** This brief should be refreshed by July 15, 2026, to capture: (a) outcome of LEED v5 for Cities second public comment, (b) any publication of LEED v5 transport-specific credit documentation requirements, and (c) registration volume data for v5 vs v4.1 under the extended window.

---

*No sourced competitor-specific positioning data is available in these source blocks. Named competitor analysis is omitted per the integrity rule. The following is structurally grounded inference.*

*Analytical inference:* Workspaces that begin building LEED v5 transport emissions documentation capability ahead of the July 2027 switchover will be positioned to respond to v5 project procurement RFQs that include emissions data requirements — a requirement that is directionally signaled by USGBC's project impact reporting roadmap, even if specific credit documentation requirements are not yet confirmed in these sources.

*Analytical inference:* The credentialing transition creates a short-term knowledge gap in the market. FACT: "The LEED professional credential exams will transition to LEED v5 content in spring 2026." *Source: LEED v5 expands: New Arc certification tools and resources for users, CAGBC/USGBC, November 3, 2025. https://www.cagbc.org/news-resources/cagbc-news/leed-v5-expands-new-arc-certification-tools-and-resources-for-users/ Until the credentialed professional workforce is established in v5 content (final exams expected late 2026), procurement specifications written by v4-credentialed professionals may not fully reflect v5 logistics documentation requirements. Workspaces that engage now with LEED v5 technical resources can position themselves ahead of that specification inflection.

*Analytical inference:* Clients managing portfolio-level LEED programs — corporate occupiers, institutional real estate holders — face a bifurcated period through June 2027 where new projects may register under either v4.1 or v5. Workspaces that can serve both tracks without documentation friction have a near-term edge over those requiring a single consistent framework.

*Industry interpretation:* The Canada Green Building Council's parallel publication of LEED v5 transition guidance signals that Canadian market clients are receiving the same transition messaging on the same timeline. *Source: CAGBC, May 27, 2026. https://www.cagbc.org/news-resources/cagbc-news/leed-v5-expands-new-arc-certification-tools-and-resources-for-users/ For workspaces active on Canada–US cross-border freight lanes, the alignment of Canadian and US transition dates reduces the complexity of serving multi-national client portfolios under a single LEED v5 framework.

---

**USGBC (U.S. Green Building Council)** is the standard-setting body and primary driver. FACT: "LEED v5 ratified by members on March 28, 2025." *Source: LEED v5, USGBC Help Center, updated May 28, 2026. https://support.usgbc.org/hc/en-us/articles/25316160948755-LEED-v5 USGBC's stated position is that "LEED v5 is USGBC's recommended path for new projects" and that it is "accelerating decarbonization, strengthening resilience and driving long-term performance worldwide." *Source: LEED v4 and v4.1 commercial registration close extended to June 30, 2027, USGBC, May 27, 2026. https://www.usgbc.org/articles/leed-v4-and-v41-commercial-registration-close-extended-june-30-2027

**GBCI (Green Business Certification Inc.)** administers credentialing. FACT: "As part of the transition from LEED v4 to LEED v5, a limited-time beta exam period will be launched for both the LEED Green Associate and LEED AP with specialty credentials." *Source: LEED v5 beta exams to launch in 2026, GBCI, January 29, 2026. https://www.gbci.org/leed-v5-beta-exams-launch-2026

**The global LEED project community** — developers, corporate occupiers, contractors, building operators — exerted direct pressure resulting in the registration extension. FACT: "This decision reflects direct feedback from you, our global LEED community." *Source: LEED v4 and v4.1 commercial registration close extended to June 30, 2027, USGBC, May 27, 2026. https://www.usgbc.org/articles/leed-v4-and-v41-commercial-registration-close-extended-june-30-2027

**CAGBC (Canada Green Building Council)** is amplifying the transition for the Canadian market, publishing parallel guidance on the Arc platform rollout and the registration extension. *Source: LEED v5 expands: New Arc certification tools and resources for users, CAGBC, November 3, 2025. https://www.cagbc.org/news-resources/cagbc-news/leed-v5-expands-new-arc-certification-tools-and-resources-for-users/ and *LEED v4/4.1 Registration Extension and Updates to Sunset Dates, CAGBC, May 27, 2026. https://www.cagbc.org/news-resources/cagbc-news/leed-v5-expands-new-arc-certification-tools-and-resources-for-users/

*Analytical inference:* The extension was not a planned pause — it was a demand-driven concession. This suggests the LEED transition is encountering real friction in the project pipeline, particularly in markets with supply chain stress. That friction is directly relevant to workspaces whose clients are managing LEED-critical procurement windows.

---

|---|-------|-------------|------|------|-----|
| 1 | LEED v5 (Help Center) | U.S. Green Building Council | Updated May 28, 2026 | Tier 2 — Regulator/standard-setter guidance | https://support.usgbc.org/hc/en-us/articles/25316160948755-LEED-v5 |
| 2 | LEED certification deadlines | U.S. Green Building Council | Current as of May 2026 | Tier 2 — Regulator/standard-setter guidance | https://www.usgbc.org/tools/leed-certification/deadlines |
| 3 | LEED v4 and v4.1 commercial registration close extended to June 30, 2027 | U.S. Green Building Council | May 27, 2026 | Tier 2 — Official announcement from standard-setter | https://www.usgbc.org/articles/leed-v4-and-v41-commercial-registration-close-extended-june-30-2027 |
| 4 | LEED v5 expands: New Arc certification tools and resources for users | Canada Green Building Council (CAGBC) / USGBC | November 3, 2025 | Tier 3 — National affiliate body announcement | https://www.cagbc.org/news-resources/cagbc-news/leed-v5-expands-new-arc-certification-tools-and-resources-for-users/ |
| 5 | LEED v5 beta exams to launch in 2026 | Green Business Certification Inc. (GBCI) | January 29, 2026 | Tier 2 — Certification body announcement | https://www.gbci.org/leed-v5-beta-exams-launch-2026 |

---

The transition from signal to structural commercial pressure follows a defined schedule with sourced milestones.

**Near-term (2026):**
- FACT: LEED v5 beta exams: LEED Green Associate beta window April 28–June 30, 2026; LEED AP with Specialty beta window June 30–August 31, 2026. *Source: LEED v5 beta exams to launch in 2026, GBCI, January 29, 2026. https://www.gbci.org/leed-v5-beta-exams-launch-2026
- FACT: "The final version of the LEED v5 exams will debut after the results of the beta period have been analyzed," toward end of 2026. *Source: LEED v5 beta exams to launch in 2026, GBCI, January 29, 2026. https://www.gbci.org/leed-v5-beta-exams-launch-2026
- FACT: LEED v5 for Cities second public comment closes June 16, 2026. *Source: LEED v5, USGBC Help Center, updated May 28, 2026. https://support.usgbc.org/hc/en-us/articles/25316160948755-LEED-v5
- FACT: In 2026, project teams can expect "Additional Project Priority credits; Expanded international guidance and alternative compliance paths; Regular addenda updates; Project impact reports." *Source: LEED v5 expands: New Arc certification tools and resources for users, CAGBC/USGBC, November 3, 2025. https://www.cagbc.org/news-resources/cagbc-news/leed-v5-expands-new-arc-certification-tools-and-resources-for-users/

**Medium-term (2027):**
- FACT: July 1, 2027: LEED v5 becomes the only version available for new commercial registrations. *Source: LEED v5, USGBC Help Center, updated May 28, 2026. https://support.usgbc.org/hc/en-us/articles/25316160948755-LEED-v5
- FACT: June 30, 2027: Registration close date for LEED v4 and v4.1 commercial systems (BD+C, ID+C, O+M, Recertification). *Source: LEED certification deadlines, USGBC. https://www.usgbc.org/tools/leed-certification/deadlines

**Long-term (2030–2033):**
- FACT: June 30, 2030: Registration close date for new volume projects referencing an existing v4/v4.1 prototype (exception pathway). *Source: LEED certification deadlines, USGBC. https://www.usgbc.org/tools/leed-certification/deadlines
- FACT: June 30, 2033: Certification sunset for all LEED v4 and v4.1 commercial rating systems. *Source: LEED certification deadlines, USGBC. https://www.usgbc.org/tools/leed-certification/deadlines

**Conversion triggers — what turns this from background signal to active commercial pressure:**

*Analytical inference:* The hardest conversion trigger is July 1, 2027. After that date, any client beginning a new commercial project enters exclusively under LEED v5, and procurement specifications for materials, components, and logistics services will increasingly reference v5 credit documentation requirements rather than v4/v4.1. Workspaces whose clients include developers, corporate occupiers, or construction managers will encounter v5-specific supply chain documentation requests starting from that date forward.

*Analytical inference:* A secondary trigger is the publication of final LEED v5 credentialing exams, expected late 2026, which will begin producing a credentialed v5 professional workforce. As that workforce grows, v5-specific procurement and logistics requirements will be specified more frequently and more precisely.

*Specific conversion timing for Cities-track projects not available from primary sources as of 2026-05-29 — the Cities second public comment closes June 16, 2026; ratification timeline has not been published.*

---

**What the workspace can credibly say:**

- LEED v4 and v4.1 registration has been extended to June 30, 2027 — clients with projects already in motion under v4/v4.1 have additional runway. This is sourced and citable.
- LEED v5 is live for new commercial registrations now (BD+C, ID+C, O+M in Arc). Clients beginning new projects in 2026 can register under v5 today.
- The certification sunset for v4/v4.1 is June 30, 2033 — projects registered before July 2027 have until mid-2033 to complete certification.
- LEED v5 project impact reports will include transportation as a tracked metric, which means transport emissions data from logistics providers will be part of what client project teams need to compile.

**Questions the workspace can pose to clients:**

- Is your project registered under v4, v4.1, or v5? (This determines which documentation framework governs your supply chain requirements.)
- Will your LEED v5 project team be using the Arc platform for documentation? If so, what transport emissions data formats does Arc accept?
- Are you aware that LEED v5 project impact reports cover transportation? Have you identified how you will source that data from your logistics providers?
- Are your LEED consultants credentialed under v4 or v5? (Credentialing transition to v5 is mid-to-late 2026 — v4 credentials remain valid but v5 exam content differs.)

**Claims to avoid:**

- Do not assert that LEED v5 mandates specific logistics emissions documentation without having reviewed the LEED v5 credit library. The transportation metric direction is sourced; specific credit requirements for logistics providers are not confirmed in these source blocks.
- Do not cite LEED v5 credit values or points for transport without sourcing them from the LEED v5 credit library directly.
- Do not represent that the workspace is "LEED v5 compliant" — LEED certification is a building-level designation, not a vendor designation.

I am with the press—who can I speak with about the release of USGBC's latest version of LEED? We welcome your interest in LEED v5. Please use the contact us form , and the submission will be directed to the appropriate person. LEED v5 transition timeline and deadlines Is the use of LEED v5 mandatory? Starting on July 1, 2027*, LEED v5 will be the only version available for new registrations for the commercial LEED BD+C, ID+C, and O+M rating systems, with limited exceptions as noted in the LEED certification deadlines page. * Last updated on May 28, 2026. When will LEED v4 and v4.1 be closed to new registrations and sunset? LEED v4 and LEED v4.1 registration close and certification sunset dates are available on the LEED certification deadlines page. Project teams can continue to register projects until a rating system's registration close date. GBCI will continue to accept initial applications (for design or standard preliminary review) for certification until a rating system's sunset date. Note: LEED BD+C and ID+C projects using the split review timeline must submit for design review by June 30, 2033, but will have an additional 18 months (until December 31, 2034) to submit for construction review*. * Last updated on May 28, 2026. What deadlines apply for projects pursuing recertification under LEED v4 O+M and LEED v4.1 O+M? Projects pursuing recertification under LEED v4 O+M or LEED v4.1 O+M must register by June 30, 2027, and submit for review by June 30, 2033*. Note that a project must have completed at least one D+C or O+M certification before it can register for recertification under LEED v4.1 O+M in Arc. * Last updated on May 28, 2026. What deadlines apply for projects using LEED v4.1 O+M: Interiors? Projects pursing certification using LEED v4.1 O+M: Interiors must register by June 30, 2027* and submit for review by June 30, 2033. * Last updated on May 28, 2026. Will projects registered under LEED v4 and LEED 4.1 have the opportunity to move to LEED v5? Yes. Contact us if LEED v5 would be a better fit for your project. Please note that requirements will differ, and work done on project documentation and forms may have to be updated should you choose to change versions. LEED v5 eligibility and certification approaches Is there guidance that provides additional details about LEED v5 Minimum Program Requirements? The LEED v5 Minimum Program Requirements (MPRs) are the same as those for LEED v4. Teams can continue to use the additional guidance provided for the MPRs in the LEED credit library and our Help Center . Are the campus, group, and volume approaches available for LEED v5 projects? LEED campus, group, and volume approaches are not yet available for LEED v5.  LEED v4 and LEED v4.1 master sites and projects within master sites must be registered by June 30, 2027*. LEED v4 or v4.1 group projects must be registered by June 30, 2027. LEED v4 or v4.1 volume prototypes must be registered by June 30, 2027. Teams can continue to register LEED v4 or v4.1 projects within existing LEED v4 or v4.1 prototypes until June 30, 2029. The certification sunset date for any of these projects will be June 30, 2033. Projects pursuing LEED volume certification should also reference the Guide to LEED Certification: Volume supplement . Go to the LEED v5 page and sign up for Technical Insider Updates for announcements as new guidance is published. * Last updated on May 28, 2026. Can residential projects use LEED v5 BD+C? Yes, although not required, a multi-family residential building with at least 4 above-grade floors can choose to pursue certification using LEED v5 BD+C. Other residential projects with 3 floors or less should use LEED v4 or LEED v4.1 as applicable. Learn more about rating systems available to residential projects. Is LEED v5 recertification currently available? Yes, LEED v5 recertification is available in Arc . Learn more about registering a LEED v5 recertification project. Are there LEED v5 requirements for LEED Zero? Not yet. The current LEED Zero program requirements are the most up-to-date. Applying LEED v5 to projects What are the fees for LEED v5? Fees for LEED v5 projects are the same as earlier versions. All LEED registration and certification fees may be found on the LEED certification fees page. How can I register a LEED v5 project? LEED v5 project registration is now available in Arc for the following rating systems: LEED v5 BD+C: New Construction LEED v5 BD+C: Core and Shell LEED v5 ID+C: Commercial Interiors LEED v5 O+M: Existing Buildings Learn more . Where can I find LEED v5 credit forms and calculators? Credit forms are available in Arc . Need to review credit forms before your project is ready for registration? Learn more about credit forms in Arc. USGBC-provided calculators are available in the LEED credit library within the "Resources and tips" tab of the applicable credit. Calculators assist project teams in demonstrating credit achievement, reducing the burden on teams to create custom methodologies. Can I submit a LEED v5 BD+C, ID+C, or O+M application for review? Project teams can apply for certification using the standard review process in Arc . Notes: Some LEED v5 O+M credit forms are still in development. If you're almost ready to submit your project with these credits, please contact us . For LEED v5 BD+C or ID+C projects, the split review process will be available soon. Where can I learn more about project priority credits? See Project priorities . Can LEED v5 credit substitutions be used for LEED v4 or LEED v4.1 projects? No. At this time, LEED v5 credit substitutions are not available for previous versions of LEED. Public comment and rating system development for LEED v5 What is the ballot approval process? Ballot approval is part of the rating system development process, and has two steps: voting/approval by consensus bodies member ratification Learn more about the process in the Foundations of LEED . What is member ratification for a new version of the LEED rating system? Member ratification is the last step in the approval process for a new version of the rating system. The rating system opens for member ratification following the public comment periods; associated updates; and approvals from the LEED Steering Committee (LSC), USGBC Board of Directors and relevant consensus committee(s). Member ratification requires a minimum of 50% of voting members supportive of adoption for the new version to continue towards market launch. Learn more about the LEED development process in the Foundations of LEED . When was the LEED v5 for Cities first public comment period? The first public comment period opened November 3, 2025 and closed January 9, 2026. When is the LEED v5 for Cities second public comment period? The second public comment period opened on May 14, 2026 and will close June 16, 2026. The draft rating system incorporates revisions based on feedback received during the first public comment period. Who can participate in the second public comment period for LEED v5 for Cities? Public comment is open to the public. Anyone may review the draft rating system and submit comments. A USGBC account is required to access the credit library and submit comments. Individuals without a USGBC account may create one. What was the timeline for the LEED v5 BD+C, ID+C, and O+M ballot approval process? USGBC on November 3, 2025 Rating System/Standard LEED LEED v5 Theme Certification updates As the building industry rapidly evolves toward a future defined by decarbonization, resilience and occupant well-being, USGBC is proud to announce the latest, most robust release of the  Arc platform  and its expanded toolkit for  LEED v5 . This significant update marks a pivotal advancement in the LEED v5 journey, unlocking certification functionality and a suite of technical resources. Take advantage of the new features, resources and tools developed to improve the user experience for project teams. LEED v5 certification functionality is now open in Arc. The Arc platform now supports exciting new certification capabilities: In addition to registering and setting up their projects, teams can explore credit forms, upload documentation and begin their certification journey. This is just the beginning—as we continue to enhance the Arc platform, more tools and resources are on the way to support your work. New and enhanced technical resources 5140 Yonge Street, certified LEED O+M: Existing Buildings v4.1, Platinum This Arc platform product release is paired with a complementary suite of additional resources to support LEED v5 project teams, including: Calculators.  The  credit library  now includes dozens of USGBC-created calculators to support credit documentation and reduce the need for bespoke calculation methods. Ongoing rating system development.  New Project Priority credits and addenda to the rating system are available in the credit library. Updated reference guide bundles.  LEED v5 reference guide bundles  available for purchase provide expanded explanations, context and updates based on user feedback from the launch preview editions. In 2026, the one-time purchase of the bundle will include robust supplementary content, such as guidance documents and sample completed resources. Additional support tools USGBC offers a variety of additional technical resources to support LEED v5 project teams. LEED v5 FAQ: Find a frequently updated database of answers for technical and practical questions in our  Help Center . LEED v5 for Operations and Maintenance resources: LEED v5 O+M project teams can access a  free scorecard builder ,  recertification guidance  and a  Guide to Strategic Decarbonization Planning  to identify their best path forward. Rating system crosswalks: Side-by-side crosswalks between  LEED v5 BD+C and SITES v2 , and between  LEED v5 and WELL  allow teams to document credits or features efficiently, maximizing synergies across systems. Professional education: To support the individual mastery of LEED v5, the LEED professional credential exams will  transition to LEED v5 content  in spring 2026. The  LEED Core Concepts Guide, 5th edition , is now available for presale to support  LEED Green Associate  exam preparation. Looking ahead USGBC will continue to expand Arc’s capabilities with new features and platform improvements in upcoming releases. In 2026, project teams can expect even more growth: Additional Project Priority credits Expanded international guidance and alternative compliance paths Regular addenda updates Project impact reports: These reports will summarize certifications using metrics on emissions, energy, water, waste, IAQ, transportation and resilience, strengthening project transparency and stakeholder communication. Registration closing and certification sunset dates Registration closing and certification sunset dates  are available to help teams plan their project timelines effectively. Continual updates and improvements LEED v5’s growing toolkit and functionality on the Arc platform is creating new pathways for technical users to manage projects, streamline certification and deliver higher sustainability performance. With new calculators, reference guides, crosswalks and planning tools, project teams are better equipped to achieve ambitious goals. Stay engaged through Arc and USGBC’s resource channels—the future of LEED v5 will be shaped by your participation and feedback. As part of the transition from LEED v4 to LEED v5 , a limited-time beta exam period will be launched for both the LEED Green Associate and LEED AP with specialty credentials. The data collection phase of the beta period offers early candidates the opportunity to engage with new exam content, provide critical feedback and access special benefits not available during the standard exam period. A beta exam is an early administration of a new credential exam, developed to ensure alignment with the most current industry standards and best practices. The LEED v5 beta exams will be available in English only and will gather data needed to refine test items and set appropriate scoring standards. Candidates participating in the beta exam will experience a delayed release of results, as response data undergoes statistical analysis necessary for finalizing the exam. The final version of the LEED v5 exams will debut after the results of the beta period have been analyzed. Beta exam pricing and schedule During the data collection phase of the beta period, candidates are eligible for a 30% discount off standard exam pricing. The data collection phase of the LEED v5 beta exams will be available only during specific windows: LEED Green Associate: April 28–June 30, 2026 LEED AP with Specialty: June 30–Aug. 31, 2026 After the data collection phase of the LEED v5 beta exams closes, the beta exam will remain available until the final exam is published, toward the end of 2026. Considerations for potential candidates The beta exam period offers a unique, limited-time opportunity for parties interested in pursuing their LEED credentials to interact with the LEED v5 content and become some of the first experts in the new version of the rating system. Advantages include Cost savings. The reduced registration fee is intended to recognize the contribution made by beta exam participants. Early access. Beta participants will engage with exam content reflecting the most recent updates to the LEED rating system. Program quality. Item analysis data from beta testers play an essential role in determining which questions perform well and help set the final passing score of the exam. The purpose of beta exam periods Beta exams serve as a critical step in credential exam development by Piloting new exam items in a live testing environment. Collecting data on question performance and overall exam difficulty. Establishing the passing score. Ensuring consistency and fairness across exam forms. Participation in the beta exam phase directly contributes to maintaining the integrity, reliability and relevance of LEED credentials. What candidates can expect Beta exam participants should anticipate several differences from the standard exam process. These include Limited testing window. Beta exams are only offered within the designated registration and testing periods. Delayed score reporting. Results will be released approximately three to four months after the close of the beta period, pending completion of statistical analyses and exam equating. Credential eligibility. Candidates who pass the beta exam will be awarded the same credential as those who pass the standard exam. Registration and additional information Registration for the LEED v5 beta exams opens in mid-February 2026. Individuals interested in participating are encouraged to thoroughly review the available information in the Help Center and assess the best pathway for their goals. sections.md:
COST ALERT

International Roadcheck 2026 ran May 12–14 across the U.S., Canada, and Mexico as a coordinated 72-hour inspection, enforcement, and data-collection initiative managed by the Commercial Vehicle Safety Alliance (CVSA). *Source: CVSA International Roadcheck Announcement, CVSA, February 12, 2026. https://cvsa.org/news/2026-roadcheck/

The event's two declared focus areas for 2026 were: (1) **driver focus — electronic logging device (ELD) tampering, falsification or manipulation**; and (2) **vehicle focus — cargo securement**. *Source: CVSA 2026 Focus Areas, CVSA, 2026. https://cvsa.org/programs/international-roadcheck/focus-area/

The selection of these focus areas was data-driven. CVSA cited that in 2025, "falsification of record of duty status was the second most-cited driver violation, at 58,382 violations. And five out of the top 10 driver violations were related to hours of service or ELDs." On cargo securement, CVSA reported that "in 2025, 18,108 violations were issued because cargo was not secured to prevent leaking/spilling/blowing/falling and 16,054 violations were issued for vehicle components or dunnage not being secured." *Source: CVSA 2026 Focus Areas, CVSA, 2026. https://cvsa.org/programs/international-roadcheck/focus-area/

The 2026 Roadcheck produced an immediate, measurable market response. According to DAT Freight & Analytics, "total load posts on DAT One rose to 4.36 million last week, up 29% from the prior week," while "equipment posts fell 12% to 186,493 as many carriers parked their trucks for the week to avoid inspection-related delays and exposure." *Source: DAT: Roadcheck week tightens capacity sharply, lifts spot rates across the board, The Trucker / DAT Freight & Analytics, May 19, 2026. https://www.thetrucker.com/trucking-news/business/dat-roadcheck-week-tightens-capacity-sharply-lifts-spot-rates-across-the-board

A compounding regulatory pressure entered the market in parallel: FMCSA has been executing a rolling programme of ELD revocations through 2026. On May 20, 2026 — the week of Roadcheck — FMCSA removed 12 ELDs from its registered list, with a replacement deadline of July 20, 2026. Prior revocations in 2026 (February, March, April, May batches) added 79+ devices to the revoked list since January 2025, each carrying a 60-day paper-log grace period followed by mandatory out-of-service enforcement. *Source: FMCSA ELD Revoked Devices News & Events, FMCSA, eld.fmcsa.dot.gov, June 2, 2026. https://eld.fmcsa.dot.gov/Support/_NewsAndEventCurrentPage

*Specific total count of all revoked devices since January 2025 not available as a single consolidated figure from primary sources as of June 2026; the 79+ figure represents a count derived from the individual revocation notices in the FMCSA source block and may understate the full tally.*

---

**1. Audit road carrier ELD compliance status — now, before July 20, 2026.**

*Action:* For every road carrier regularly used for drayage and surface legs — particularly smaller or specialist carriers used for high-value automotive, fine art, and live events freight — confirm their ELD device is on FMCSA's current registered ELD list and is not among the revoked devices. The July 20, 2026 OOS deadline for the May 20 revocation batch is the nearest hard enforcement date.
*Why now:* Carriers on revoked devices have until July 20 to replace them; if they have not, any shipment moving on their trucks after that date is at OOS risk. For time-sensitive verticals, a mid-haul OOS stop is a client-relationship event, not just a cost event.
*Source: FMCSA ELD Revoked Devices News & Events, FMCSA, June 2, 2026. https://eld.fmcsa.dot.gov/Support/_NewsAndEventCurrentPage

**2. Revise road-mode rate assumptions in client-facing quotes and internal budgets.**

*Analytical inference:* *Action:* Reset road-mode spot rate assumptions to reflect the current market: dry van at ~$2.58/mile, reefer at ~$3.05/mile, flatbed at ~$3.16/mile as of Roadcheck week (broker-to-carrier averages). These are not the ceiling but they are the confirmed recent floor during a capacity-constrained period. The 30% y/y structural increase makes pre-2026 rate tables a margin risk.
*Why now:* ACT Research flags that equipment cost increases are expected in 2027, and the driver availability index (30.4) is at a cycle-turning level. Quoting road legs at 2024 or early-2025 rates exposes margin.
*Source: DAT / The Trucker, May 19, 2026; ACT Research, May 22, 2026.*

**3. Build pre-Roadcheck freight planning into the annual live events and film calendar.**

*Action:* Add Roadcheck (historically mid-May, 72-hour window) to the annual capacity-planning calendar for road-dependent cargo. For live events and film productions with May show dates or location-move windows, tender road legs the week before Roadcheck rather than during it. This captures contract coverage before the spot market tightens.
*Why now:* DAT confirmed that "some shippers move tendering up to the week before" Roadcheck; "others lose contract coverage as carriers decline loads and freight rolls to spot." Proactive tendering is a structured response to a predictable annual event.
*Source: DAT / The Trucker, May 19, 2026. https://www.thetrucker.com/trucking-news/business/dat-roadcheck-week-tightens-capacity-sharply-lifts-spot-rates-across-the-board

**4. Monitor CVSA Roadcheck 2026 results when published (expected Q3 2026).**

*Action:* Set a re-check for Q3 2026 when CVSA releases inspection data, OOS rates, and violation breakdowns. If ELD and cargo securement OOS rates rose materially above the 2025 baselines, it signals sustained enforcement intensity into Roadcheck 2027 and further justifies pre-positioning road capacity.
*Source: CVSA International Roadcheck Announcement, CVSA, February 12, 2026. https://cvsa.org/news/2026-roadcheck/

**5. Evaluate carrier safety data tooling.**

*Action:* The FreightWaves SONAR Carrier Safety Dashboard launched May 12, 2026. Evaluate whether a subscription provides actionable pre-shipment carrier screening capability for the workspace's road procurement workflow.
*Source: FreightWaves homepage / SONAR announcement, FreightWaves, May 12, 2026. https://freightwaves.com/

---

COST ALERT

The workspace — operating primarily on air freight with road as a secondary mode, moving time-sensitive cargo verticals including live events, fine art, luxury goods, film and TV, and high-value automotive — uses road for drayage, last-mile, and cross-country surface legs connecting to air gateways. The following cost signals apply to road-mode procurement.

**Spot rate movement — confirmed actuals for Roadcheck week:**

- Dry van: $2.58 per mile (7-day average broker-to-carrier), up 21 cents week over week
- Refrigerated: $3.05 per mile, up 32 cents week over week
- Flatbed: $3.16 per mile, up 10 cents week over week
- Dry van load-to-truck ratio: 13.38, up from 8.70 the prior week
- Reefer load-to-truck ratio: 27.60, up from 16.25
- Flatbed load-to-truck ratio: 88.82, up from 62.93

*Source: DAT: Roadcheck week tightens capacity sharply, lifts spot rates across the board, The Trucker / DAT Freight & Analytics, May 19, 2026. https://www.thetrucker.com/trucking-news/business/dat-roadcheck-week-tightens-capacity-sharply-lifts-spot-rates-across-the-board

*Analytical inference:* **Year-on-year rate context:** ACT Research documents "the current 30% y/y increase in truckload spot rates, net fuel, coming out of Roadcheck." *Source: ACT Research Freight Forecast Blog — A Supply-Driven Freight Cycle, ACT Research, May 22, 2026. https://www.actresearch.net/resources/blog/freight-forecast-blog

*Operational implication:* For workspaces routing high-value, time-sensitive cargo (live events equipment, fine art, film production freight) on road legs booked on the spot market, a 21–32 cent per-mile rate spike during Roadcheck week is not the primary risk — shipment delay and missed pickup windows are. The OOS mechanism (a Level I inspection takes "45 minutes to an hour per truck when nothing's wrong") compounds the time exposure for cargo that has hard delivery windows. *Source: DAT: Roadcheck week tightens capacity sharply, lifts spot rates across the board, The Trucker / DAT Freight & Analytics, May 19, 2026. https://www.thetrucker.com/trucking-news/business/dat-roadcheck-week-tightens-capacity-sharply-lifts-spot-rates-across-the-board

*Operational implication:* Flatbed equipment saw the sharpest capacity withdrawal (down 20% in equipment posts), with a load-to-truck ratio of 88.82 during Roadcheck week. For cargo verticals that may route oversized or special-dimension freight (high-value automotive, large-format live events rigs, film production equipment) on flatbed, the tightening is acute.

*Operational implication:* The structural rate environment — 30% y/y increase attributable to capacity reduction, not volume growth — means the Roadcheck week spike does not return entirely to its pre-Roadcheck baseline if the underlying capacity constraint (driver availability at 30.4 index, equipment fleet below replacement sales for over a year) persists. The workspace should not anchor road-rate budgets to pre-2026 baselines.

*Specific forward rate trajectory not available from primary sources as of June 2026; ACT Research characterises the cycle as "likely supporting a longer than normal cycle" but does not publish a specific rate forecast in the source block available.*

---

*Analytical inference:* Workspaces with pre-positioned road carrier relationships — carriers operating compliant ELDs on the current FMCSA registered list, with clean CSA scores and up-to-date cargo securement training — are less exposed to capacity withdrawal during Roadcheck and similar enforcement events than workspaces relying on the spot market or on carriers operating in the small-fleet segment most represented in revocation lists.

*Analytical inference:* The FMCSA revocation lists are concentrated in smaller ELD providers with names indicating small-fleet or owner-operator market positioning (e.g., Sam Freight ELD, First ELD, Club ELD, Hero ELD). Large national carriers operating enterprise-grade ELD systems are structurally less exposed to revocation-driven OOS risk. Workspaces whose carrier base skews toward owner-operators and small fleets — common in specialist cargo verticals (fine art, high-value automotive, film equipment) where dedicated/white-glove carriers are preferred — face higher residual compliance exposure than workspaces routing through large asset-based carriers. *Source for revocation list composition: FMCSA ELD Revoked Devices News & Events, FMCSA, eld.fmcsa.dot.gov, June 2, 2026. https://eld.fmcsa.dot.gov/Support/_NewsAndEventCurrentPage

The FreightWaves SONAR platform launched a Carrier Safety Dashboard on May 12, 2026 — the first day of Roadcheck — described as "a comprehensive intelligence tool" providing "FMCSA and CSA intelligence." *Source: FreightWaves homepage / SONAR announcement, FreightWaves, May 12, 2026. https://freightwaves.com/ 

*Analytical inference:* Freight forwarders and brokers with access to real-time CSA and safety scoring intelligence gain a procurement edge during enforcement-heavy periods — they can route away from carriers at OOS risk before a shipment is disrupted. Workspaces without such tooling are flying blind on carrier compliance posture during peak enforcement windows.

*Named competitor positioning on carrier safety tooling is not available from the source blocks; no claims are made about specific competitors' access or contractual relationships.*

---

| 7 | FreightWaves homepage / SONAR Carrier Safety Dashboard launch | FreightWaves | May 12, 2026 | Tier 5 — Trade press / product announcement | https://freightwaves.com/ |

---

The Roadcheck-week capacity contraction is historically temporary. DAT's Dean Croke stated: "This typically reverses the following week as parked capacity returns and pulled-forward freight is already covered." *Source: DAT: Roadcheck week tightens capacity sharply, lifts spot rates across the board, The Trucker / DAT Freight & Analytics, May 19, 2026. https://www.thetrucker.com/trucking-news/business/dat-roadcheck-week-tightens-capacity-sharply-lifts-spot-rates-across-the-board

However, the post-Roadcheck 2026 rate picture sits inside a larger structural shift. ACT Research documents that the ACT For-Hire Driver Availability Index fell to 30.4 in April 2026, compared to being above 50 — "a surfeit, rather than a shortage" — continuously from June 2022 to December 2025 (43 consecutive months). Denoyer stated: "The past two rate cycles started around the time this index fell below 40." The index fell below 40 following new non-domicile CDL rules that took effect in mid-March 2026: "As the new nondomicile CDL rules took effect in mid-March, the ACT Driver Availability Index tightened 4.8 points, to 35.0 in March from 39.8 in February." *Source: ACT Research Freight Forecast Blog — A Supply-Driven Freight Cycle, ACT Research, May 22, 2026. https://www.actresearch.net/resources/blog/freight-forecast-blog

The next concrete enforcement trigger with market-moving potential is the **July 20, 2026 OOS deadline** for motor carriers still operating the 12 ELDs revoked on May 20, 2026. Carriers who have not replaced those devices face out-of-service citation from that date. *Source: FMCSA ELD Revoked Devices News & Events, FMCSA, eld.fmcsa.dot.gov, June 2, 2026. https://eld.fmcsa.dot.gov/Support/_NewsAndEventCurrentPage

The HERO ELD out-of-service deadline has already passed: "As of June 2, 2026, safety officials who encounter a driver using the below revoked ELD, or improperly using paper logs, should cite 395.8(a)(1) and place the driver out-of-service." *Source: FMCSA ELD Revoked Devices News & Events, FMCSA, eld.fmcsa.dot.gov, June 2, 2026. https://eld.fmcsa.dot.gov/Support/_NewsAndEventCurrentPage

*Analytical inference:* Three signals — the Roadcheck-week capacity contraction, the rolling ELD revocation OOS deadlines through July 2026, and the structural driver availability decline — are not individually sufficient to sustain rate elevation, but their simultaneous presence in Q2 2026 raises the probability that the post-Roadcheck rate normalization is shallower and slower than the historical one-week reversal pattern.

The **CVSA Roadcheck 2026 results** — inspection counts, OOS rates, violation breakdowns — are scheduled to be released later in 2026. *Source: CVSA International Roadcheck Announcement, CVSA, February 12, 2026. https://cvsa.org/news/2026-roadcheck/ These results will indicate whether the ELD and cargo securement focus areas generated higher OOS rates than the 2025 baselines (18.4% vehicles OOS, 5.9% drivers OOS in 2025), and whether the enforcement intensity has increased. *Source: International Roadcheck 2026: ELDs under scrutiny, FreightWaves, February 14, 2026. https://www.freightwaves.com/news/international-roadcheck-2026-elds-under-scrutiny

**Re-check window: July 20, 2026** (next ELD OOS enforcement wave); **Q3 2026** for CVSA Roadcheck results publication.

---

**What the workspace can credibly say:**

- International Roadcheck 2026 ran May 12–14 and produced a measurable, documented capacity contraction: load posts up 29%, equipment posts down 12%, with spot rates rising 21–32 cents per mile across equipment types. These are DAT Freight & Analytics figures, sourced from live market data.
- The rate increase is occurring inside a larger structural shift: ACT Research documents a 30% year-on-year increase in truckload spot rates net of fuel coming out of Roadcheck, driven by a driver availability index that has fallen to 30.4 — below the threshold (40) that preceded the last two rate cycles.
- The workspace screens its road carriers for ELD compliance and CSA standing. In an enforcement environment where FMCSA has revoked 79+ ELD devices since early 2025, carrier selection matters. Carriers on revoked devices face out-of-service orders that can strand a load for hours or longer.
- For cargo with hard delivery windows — live events, film production, exhibition openings — the workspace plans road legs outside peak Roadcheck timing or uses carriers with demonstrated clean inspection records.

**Questions to pose to clients:**

- Does your current 3PL or road broker confirm the ELD compliance status of the carriers it books for your time-sensitive freight? If not, the window of July 20, 2026 (next OOS deadline) is a credible reason to ask.
- Have you experienced rate increases or capacity gaps on road legs in May? The data shows this is structural, not just a Roadcheck blip.

**Pitfalls to avoid:**

*Analytical inference:* - Do not claim the workspace has visibility into every carrier's CSA score in real time unless that tooling is confirmed and in operation.
- Do not characterise the rate spike as permanent or the rate normalisation as certain — both the spike and the recovery are data-bounded and neither direction can be guaranteed beyond what the sourced analysis states.
- Do not cite the 30% y/y rate figure as a forward forecast; it is an observed trailing measure reported by ACT Research as of May 22, 2026.

---

**CVSA** is the multi-jurisdictional non-profit alliance of commercial motor vehicle safety officials from Canada, Mexico, and the U.S. that organises and coordinates Roadcheck. CVSA's stated mission is to improve commercial motor vehicle safety and enforcement. Its focus-area selection — ELD integrity and cargo securement — reflects enforcement data from the prior year and is intended to direct inspector attention toward the highest-frequency violations. *Source: CVSA International Roadcheck Announcement, CVSA, February 12, 2026. https://cvsa.org/news/2026-roadcheck/

**FMCSA** is the U.S. federal regulator responsible for the ELD mandate (49 CFR Part 395, Appendix A to Subpart B). The rolling revocation programme is FMCSA's mechanism for enforcing minimum technical standards on registered ELD providers. When a device fails those standards, FMCSA removes it from the registered list; motor carriers using a revoked device face an out-of-service citation under 49 CFR 395.8(a)(1) once the 60-day grace period ends. *Source: FMCSA ELD Revoked Devices News & Events, FMCSA, eld.fmcsa.dot.gov, June 2, 2026. https://eld.fmcsa.dot.gov/Support/_NewsAndEventCurrentPage

**DAT Freight & Analytics** has documented the market mechanics, with Dean Croke, industry analyst at DAT, stating: "The CVSA International Roadcheck inspection event usually has an outsized effect on truckload capacity and spot rates, with load posts rising and truck posts declining by double-digit percentages." *Source: DAT: Roadcheck week tightens capacity sharply, lifts spot rates across the board, The Trucker / DAT Freight & Analytics, May 19, 2026. https://www.thetrucker.com/trucking-news/business/dat-roadcheck-week-tightens-capacity-sharply-lifts-spot-rates-across-the-board

**ACT Research** frames the broader structural context: "The current 30% y/y increase in truckload spot rates, net fuel, coming out of Roadcheck, is driven primarily by tighter capacity." ACT Research Vice President Tim Denoyer noted: "New FMCSA regulations have acted as a catalyst, and seem likely to result in tighter capacity and higher rates from here." *Source: ACT Research Freight Forecast Blog — A Supply-Driven Freight Cycle, ACT Research, May 22, 2026. https://www.actresearch.net/resources/blog/freight-forecast-blog

*Analytical inference:* The alignment of CVSA's enforcement focus with FMCSA's concurrent ELD revocation activity creates a reinforcing pressure on carriers already managing device-compliance uncertainty. Carriers whose ELDs were recently revoked, or whose drivers were flagged for ELD manipulation at inspections, face both an out-of-service risk and a market where replacement capacity is priced higher.

---

CVSA’s International Roadcheck Scheduled for May 12-14 - CVSA – Commercial Vehicle Safety Alliance Skip to Content Search for: Search Exit Search English Français Español About Contacts Search Member Login English Français Español Inspections Training Programs Events News Sponsorship Store About Contacts Member Login Search for: Search News Archives 2026 2025 2024 CVSA’s International Roadcheck Scheduled for May 12-14 February 12, 2026 From May 12 to 14, enforcement personnel throughout North America will inspect commercial motor vehicles and commercial motor vehicle drivers for compliance with vehicle, cargo and driver regulatory requirements as part of the Commercial Vehicle Safety Alliance’s (CVSA) 72-hour inspection, enforcement and data-collection initiative, International Roadcheck. During International Roadcheck, inspectors at weigh/inspection stations and pop-up inspection sites primarily conduct the North American Standard Level I Inspection , a 37-step procedure that includes two major parts – an examination of the driver’s operating requirements and an assessment of the vehicle’s mechanical fitness. For the driver portion of the inspection, inspectors check the driver’s qualifications, license, record of duty status, medical examiner’s certificate, seat belt usage, skill performance evaluation certificate (if applicable), and status in the Drug and Alcohol Clearinghouse (in the U.S.). Inspectors also look for signs of alcohol and/or drug impairment. If an inspector identifies driver out-of-service violations, they will place the driver out of service, restricting that driver from operating their vehicle. For the vehicle portion of the inspection, inspectors assess the vehicle’s brake systems, cargo securement, coupling devices, driveline/driveshaft components, driver’s seat, fuel and exhaust systems, frames, lighting devices, steering mechanisms, suspensions, tires, wheels, rims, hubs, and windshield wipers. Inspections of motorcoaches/buses and other passenger-carrying commercial motor vehicles also include examination of emergency exits, seating, and electrical cables and systems in the engine and battery compartments. If out-of-service violations are found during an inspection, the vehicle will be placed out of service and restricted from movement until all out-of-service violations have been properly addressed. A vehicle that successfully passes a Level I or V Inspection without any critical vehicle inspection item violations may receive a CVSA decal , which is valid for up to three months. A valid decal signals to commercial motor vehicle enforcement personnel that the vehicle was recently inspected and did not have out-of-service violations. Each year, International Roadcheck places special emphasis on a driver violation category and a vehicle violation category to highlight those aspects of an inspection. The driver focus for this year’s International Roadcheck is on electronic logging device (ELD) tampering, falsification or manipulation. During an inspection, the inspector will review the driver’s record of duty status as usual and check for false or manipulated entries, with a focus on ELD tampering. Inaccurate ELD entries may result from a driver’s lack of understanding of the federal regulations and exemptions. However, in some cases, inaccurate entries are purposefully used to conceal hours-of-service violations, and some records are manipulated to conceal driving time (with no indication the record was edited as required by federal regulations). Last year , falsification of record of duty status was the second most-cited driver violation, at 58,382 violations. And five out of the top 10 driver violations were related to hours of service or ELDs. This year’s International Roadcheck vehicle focus is cargo securement. Improper or inadequate cargo securement poses a serious risk to the driver and other motorists by adversely affecting the vehicle’s maneuverability and/or causing unsecured loads to fall or become dislodged, resulting in roadway hazards and/or crashes. In 2025 , 18,108 violations were issued because cargo was not secured to prevent leaking/spilling/blowing/falling and 16,054 violations were issued for vehicle components or dunnage not being secured. During the 72 hours of International Roadcheck, data will be collected, and the results will be released later this year. CVSA is a nonprofit organization composed of local, state, provincial, territorial and federal commercial motor vehicle safety officials and industry representatives in Canada, Mexico and the U.S. The Alliance aims to prevent commercial motor vehicle crashes, injuries and fatalities and believes that collaboration between government and industry improves road safety and saves lives. Its mission is to improve commercial motor vehicle safety and enforcement by providing guidance, education and advocacy for enforcement and industry across North America. (Photo: Jim Allen\FreightWaves) International Roadcheck will be May 12-14 this year, and ELDs will be the primary driver safety target. The separate vehicle safety target will be cargo securement. The Commercial Vehicle Safety Alliance, which manages Roadcheck, announced the dates of the 72-hour enforcement late this past week. The dates are in line with when International Roadcheck generally takes place. Roadcheck last year was May 13-15. Roadcheck is referred to as “international” because it takes place in the U.S., Canada and Mexico in a coordinated effort among law enforcement. Inspectors, according to CVSA, are at weigh stations or inspections as well as “pop-up inspection sites.” The inspection is a 37-point test. The two major parts, CVSA said, are “an examination of the driver’s operating requirements and an assessment of the vehicle’s mechanical fitness.” Tampering, falsification or manipulation The driver focus in 2026 be ELDs, with inspectors looking for “tampering, falsification or manipulation,” according to CVSA. “Inaccurate ELD entries may result from a driver’s lack of understanding of the federal regulations and exemptions,” CVSA said in its announcement. “However, in some cases, inaccurate entries are purposefully used to conceal hours-of-service violations, and some records are manipulated to conceal driving time (with no indication the record was edited as required by federal regulations).” CVSA said in 2025, falsification of records was one of the most cited violations during all roadside inspections recorded by FMCSA , with more than 50,000 booked by the agency over the course of the year.  CVSA said of the “vehicle focus” that improper or inadequate cargo securement “poses a serious risk to the driver and other motorists by adversely affecting the vehicle’s maneuverability and/or causing unsecured loads to fall or become dislodged, resulting in roadway hazards and/or crashes.” FMCSA data from last year, according to CVSA, recorded 18,108 violations in the U.S. during the year “issued because cargo was not secured to prevent leaking/spilling/blowing/falling and 16,054 violations were issued for vehicle components or dunnage not being secured.” Last year, CVSA made 56,178 inspections during Roadcheck. Of those inspections, 81.6% of the vehicles and 94.1% of the drivers passed the inspection. Others received an out of service order. Roadcheck last year was the first time in several years when the number of drivers who stayed off the road to avoid stepped-up enforcement appeared to have a noticeable impact on capacity. It had been seen as a possible first sign to the end of the freight recession. DAT: Roadcheck week tightens capacity sharply, lifts spot rates across the board - TheTrucker.com Skip to content Home Trucking News The Nation Business Trucking Life Equipment & Tech Truck Driving Job News Highway Angels Podcasts Perspective Ask the Attorney Insurance Insights Mind Over Matter Owner Operator Guide Rhythm of the Road Security Pit Stop The Trucker Trainer Veterans’ Corner Jobs All Truck Driving Jobs   Driver Jobs by State   Driver Jobs by Type   Driver Jobs by Carrier Diesel Mechanic Jobs Job Resources Truck Driving Job News Truck Driving Job Resource Videos Trucking Industry History and Overview Trucking Industry Information by State Truck Driving FAQs Diesel Mechanic Job Resources CDL Training Schools Truckload Authority Truckload Authority News   Government Affairs   Trends in Trucking   National Newsmakers   Chat with the Chairman   Talking TCA   Highway Angels  Truckload Authority Magazine  Subscribe About TCA Business Truck Driving Job News DAT: Roadcheck week tightens capacity sharply, lifts spot rates across the board By Dana Guthrie - May 19, 2026 post Home   >   Business • Truck Driving Job News   >   DAT: Roadcheck week tightens capacity sharply, lifts spot rates across the board Reading Time: 2 minutes Roadcheck squeezes capacity, drives spot rates upward, according to DAT Freight & Analytics. Facebook Twitter Email Share BLOOMINGTON, Ind. — Total load posts on DAT One rose to 4.36 million last week, up 29% from the prior week , as brokers pushed freight into the spot market during CVSA’s annual International Roadcheck inspection event. [ “Equipment posts fell 12% to 186,493 as many carriers parked their trucks for the week to avoid inspection-related delays and exposure,” DAT Freight & Analytics said. “The capacity pullback drove national 7-day average broker-to-carrier spot rates higher across all three equipment types.” The Roadcheck Effect “The CVSA International Roadcheck inspection event usually has an outsized effect on truckload capacity and spot rates, with load posts rising and truck posts declining by double-digit percentages,” said Dean Croke, industry analyst, DAT. According to Croke, several things happen at once during Roadcheck week: Carriers park trucks to avoid exposure. Drivers who think their vehicle or paperwork might not pass, or who simply don’t want to risk an out-of-service order that strands them for hours or days, take the week off. This is why equipment posts drop sharply (down 12% across all three equipment types last week, with flatbed down 20%). Behaviors change. The capacity drop during Roadcheck is real but somewhat behavioral. Many carriers are still running, just being more selective about loads, lanes, and inspection-heavy corridors. Last week’s truck-post counts likely overstate the physical capacity loss but accurately reflect the market dynamic that spot rates respond to. Productivity falls for trucks that stay on the road. Even compliant carriers lose hours to inspections themselves. A Level I inspection is a 37-step procedure, which typically takes 45 minutes to an hour per truck when nothing’s wrong. Multiply that across weigh stations and pop-up sites, and effective capacity tightens further than the post counts suggest. Last year, CVSA officials conducted 56,178 inspections across the United States, Canada, and Mexico. That’s approximately 13 vehicles per minute during the 72-hour window. Schedules shift. With capacity expected to be scarce, some shippers move tendering up to the week before; others lose contract coverage as carriers decline loads and freight rolls to spot. Both dynamics inflate spot load posts (up 29% across the three equipment types last week). 7-Day Average Broker-to-Carrier Spot Rates ▲ Dry van: $2.58 per mile, up 21 cents week over week ▲ Refrigerated: $3.05 per mile, up 32 cents ▲ Flatbed: $3.16 per mile, up 10 cents Van: Capacity Exits, Rates Jump ▲ Van loads: 1,793,675, up 36% week over week ▼ Van equipment: 134,079, down 11% ▲ Linehaul rate: $2.22 per mile, up 21 cents week over week ▲ Load-to-truck ratio: 13.38, up from 8.70 the prior week Reefer: Roadcheck and Produce Season Collide ▲ Reefer loads: 940,747, up 50% week over week ▼ Reefer equipment: 34,083, down 12% ▲ Linehaul rate: $2.68 per mile, up 32 cents ▲ Load-to-truck ratio: 27.60, up from 16.25 Flatbed: Sharpest Capacity Drop of the Three ▲ Flatbed loads: 1,628,127, up 13% week over week ▼ Flatbed equipment: 18,331, down 20% ▲ Linehaul rate: $2.79 per mile, up 10 cents ▲ Load-to-truck ratio: 88.82, up from 62.93 “The net effect is a textbook tightening: more demand chasing less supply,” Croke said. “This typically reverses the following week as parked capacity returns and pulled-forward freight is already covered.” Dana Guthrie Dana Guthrie is an award-winning journalist who has been featured in multiple newspapers, books and magazines across the globe. this A supply-driven freight cycle doesn’t imply strong volumes, and this time is no different. The current 30% y/y increase in truckload spot rates, net fuel, coming out of Roadcheck, is driven primarily by tighter capacity, as discussed in the latest release of the Freight Forecast: Rate and Volume OUTLOOK report. DAT US Dry Van Spot Rates & Driver Availability “Improving survey data, including a jump in the ACT For-Hire Volume Index, suggest our friends at medium and large dry van and reefer fleets are beginning to see significantly stronger demand, even as the broader market does not,” said Tim Denoyer, ACT Research’s Vice President and Senior Analyst. “The source of this early demand increase is primarily capacity reduction, which has accelerated this year due to an incipient driver shortage.” “While the goods economy is providing little lift, the key question becomes, how bad will the driver situation get? In a word, worse. Truckload spot rates have risen materially in recent months as the ACT For-Hire Driver Availability Index has declined. This index was above 50, meaning a surfeit, rather than a shortage, from June 2022 to December 2025, 43 straight months. It fell to 30.4 in April. New FMCSA regulations have acted as a catalyst, and seem likely to result in tighter capacity and higher rates from here,” Denoyer concluded. Freight Forecast Report Overview The monthly 58-page ACT freight forecast provides analysis and forecasts for a broad range of U.S. freight measures, including the Cass Freight Index, Cass Truckload Linehaul Index, and DAT spot and contract rates by trailer type. The service provides monthly, quarterly, and annual predictions for the TL, LTL, and intermodal markets over a two- to three-year time horizon, including capacity, volumes, and rates. The Freight Forecast provides unmatched detail on the freight rate outlook, helping companies across the supply chain plan with greater visibility and less uncertainty. ACT Research Overview ACT Research is recognized as the leading publisher of commercial vehicle truck, trailer, and bus industry data, market analysis and forecasts for the North America and China markets. ACT’s analytical services are used by all major North American truck and trailer manufacturers and their suppliers, as well as banking and investment companies. ACT Research is a contributor to the Blue Chip Economic Indicators and a member of the Wall Street Journal Economic Forecast Panel. ACT Research executives have received peer recognition, including election to the Board of Directors of the National Association for Business Economics, appointment as Consulting Economist to the National Private Truck Council, and the Lawrence R. Klein Award for Blue Chip Economic Indicators’ Most Accurate Economic Forecast over a four-year period. ACT Research senior staff members have earned accolades including Chicago Federal Reserve Automotive Outlook Symposium Best Overall Forecast, Wall Street Journal Top Economic Outlook, and USA Today Top 10 Economic Forecasters. More information can be found at www.actresearch.net . Additional Resources Driver Shortage Begins The US trucking industry hasn’t had a driver shortage in four years, but recent regulatory changes have accelerated the tightening, supporting higher freight rates, as discussed in the latest release of the Freight Forecast: Rate and Volume OUTLOOK report. “Spot truckload rates have been rising significantly for several months driven by several factors, but we see the return to driver shortage as a critical factor as the industry prepares for Roadcheck,” said Tim Denoyer, ACT Research’s Vice President and Senior Analyst. “After a four-year bottoming phase of the for-hire cycle, we believe tighter supply has moved us to the early cycle phase where capacity has become short, pressing rates higher.” “In addition to new Class 8 tractor sales below levels needed to sustain the fleet for over a year now, our survey of medium and large fleets shows we have entered another driver shortage, the third in the past decade. As the new nondomicile CDL rules took effect in mid-March, the ACT Driver Availability Index tightened 4.8 points, to 35.0 in March from 39.8 in February. “Driver availability is a key component of capacity in the market, and additional scarcity seems likely, supporting higher freight rates. The past two rate cycles started around the time this index fell below 40. With effects of regulations likely to increase and equipment costs set to rise in 2027, it will be a massive challenge to turn the tide of tightening capacity, likely supporting a longer than normal cycle, in our view. “While the TL driver shortage is front and center, we also added six new intermodal volume forecasts this month, with thanks to our new partners at the Intermodal Association of North America (IANA),” Denoyer concluded.
